report_name: CISA Publishes Guide for Using Cyber Decoys to Detect Intruders

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Mentioned as a technique used by stealthy attackers that cyber decoys, such as disabled administrator accounts, are designed to detect.

attack_patterns.name: Account Discovery
attack_patterns.description: Mentioned as a likely adversary behavior where decoys like fake user accounts would be discovered and interacted with, generating an alert.

attack_patterns.name: OS Credential Dumping
attack_patterns.description: Implied as a method through which attackers might find decoy credentials, such as a fake AWS key placed in a configuration file, which a honeytoken is designed to detect.

attack_patterns.name: File and Directory Discovery
attack_patterns.description: Implied by the use of 'breadcrumbs' and 'tripwires' like a file named `passwords.txt` on a file share, which are designed to be found by attackers performing file system discovery.

identities.name: U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
identities.description: The U.S. government agency that published the guidance on using cyber decoys for threat detection and response.

identities.name: U.S. critical infrastructure operators
identities.description: The primary audience for CISA's cyber decoy guidance, encouraged to adopt these strategies to enhance threat detection.

indicators.name: Honeytoken AWS API Key Usage
indicators.pattern:
title: Honeytoken AWS API Key Usage
id: f1a2b3c4-d5e6-4f7a-8b9c-0d1e2f3a4b5c
status: experimental
description: Detects the usage of a known-bad, decoy AWS API key (honeytoken). Any activity from this key is a high-fidelity indicator of compromise. Replace the placeholder key with your actual honeytoken key ID.
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/resources-tools/resources/using-cyber-decoys-strengthen-detection-and-response
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-17
tags:
  - attack.t1078.004
  - attack.credential_access
level: critical
logsource:
  service: cloudtrail
  product: aws
detection:
  selection:
    userIdentity.accessKeyId: 'ASIAXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' # Placeholder for a decoy AWS access key ID
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the usage of a decoy AWS access key (honeytoken) by monitoring AWS CloudTrail logs, as recommended in CISA's guidance. Any use of this key is a definitive sign of compromise.

indicators.name: Decoy User Account Authentication Attempt
indicators.pattern:
title: Decoy User Account Authentication Attempt
id: e2f3a4b5-c6d7-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b
status: experimental
description: Detects authentication attempts using a known decoy user account. Any logon attempt with this account is a high-fidelity indicator of compromise. Replace placeholder names with your actual decoy account names.
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/resources-tools/resources/using-cyber-decoys-strengthen-detection-and-response
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-17
tags:
  - attack.t1078
  - attack.t1087
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.discovery
level: high
logsource:
  category: authentication
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetUserName:
      - 'backup-admin'
      - 'sql-svc-decoy'
      - 'testuser01'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects authentication attempts using a known decoy user account, such as a disabled administrator account. This aligns with CISA's guidance on using honeytokens for early threat detection.

indicators.name: Tripwire Canary File Access
indicators.pattern:
title: Tripwire Canary File Access
id: d3e4f5a6-b7c8-4d9a-8b0c-1d2e3f4a5b6c
status: experimental
description: Detects access to a tripwire or canary file/share. Any access to these decoy resources is a high-fidelity indicator of compromise. Replace placeholders with your actual canary file paths.
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/resources-tools/resources/using-cyber-decoys-strengthen-detection-and-response
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-17
tags:
  - attack.t1083
  - attack.discovery
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\\FileServer\Finance\passwords.txt'
      - '\\corp\secrets\credentials.xlsx'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects when an attacker accesses a decoy file or network share (a 'tripwire' or 'breadcrumb'), as described in CISA's guidance. This provides a high-fidelity alert for discovery activity.

relationships.source_name: U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
